newsitem.title: USA: Dow sees flight to quality, techs depress Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Dow sees flight to quality, techs depress Nasdaq.

text.p: The Dow industrial average made a resilient push higher by midday on Tuesday after losing ground at the opening, but Nasdaq remained depressed by concerns surrounding the technology sector.
The Dow was up about 50 points, or 0.69 percent, at 7340, after hitting a session low of 7254.
The rise by the blue chips prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set trading curbs at 1206 EDT/1606 GMT.
"Investors are using any dips as buying opportunities and this is a snap-back from yesterday's declines," said Sam Stovall, an analyst at S&P Industry Reports.
Analysts said investors were trying to position themselves ahead of a key U.S. employment report due out on Friday.

"The Dow is benefiting from a nice, even distribution of buying," Charles Payne, an analyst at Wall Street Strategist said. "There is a flight to quality. Investors are trying to position themselves in good long-term places, in case the market gets rocky."
But Nasdaq was off about 10 points at 1396, dragged down by losses in networking and disk drive makers, as well as Intel Corp, the leading maker of computer chips.
Shares of technology companies retreated after news from both Seagate Technology Inc and Cabletron Systems Inc that their quarterly earnings would be below forecast.
Intel was down four at 145-3/4. Last week, it said its second-quarter earnings would fall short of expectations because of weaker demand, especially in Europe.
"Intel is still under pressure and that has dampened enthusiasm for techs," one trader said.
Seagate was off 3-1/2 at 38-7/8 while Cabletron was off 15-1/8 at 30-5/8. A selloff in Cabletron shares triggered declines in other networking stocks.
Bay Networks Inc was off 2-1/8 at 22-1/4, Cisco Systems Inc was off 2-9/16 at 65-1/4 and 3Coms Corp was down 3-7/16 at 45-5/8.
But smaller and middle-capitalization shares continued to perform reasonably well, analysts said.
The Standard & Poor's index was up 2.65 points at 849.03 while the Russell 2000 index of smaller capitalization issues was barely changed, off 0.04 points at 383.

"It's obvious that there is money out there that still wants to go into stocks and investors fear not participating in a market rise," Legg Mason Wood Walker chief market strategist Richard Cripps said.
The long bond also strengthened, giving support to stocks. It was up 6/32 at a 6.89 percent yield.

Among big-capitalization stocks, financial, oil and drug stocks were mildly stronger, and consumer products company Procter & Gamble Co recovered from a rating downgrade on Monday by Smith Barney, analysts said.
Procter & Gamble was up 1-5/8 at 135-1/4.
Among other active issues, shares in health care provider Humana Inc climbed after the company announced it would acquire Physician Corp of America for $400 million.
By early afternoon, Humana stock was up 5/8 at 23-7/8 while Physician Corp was up 3/8 at 6-5/8.
